block.comment: Purpose: The built-in LED blinks immediately after upload. Plotter creates controls for interval, on-time, enable, pattern and a text reply from the board. Wiring: Only the Pro Mini and USB–Serial adapter; L / D13 is built in. Try: Try a slower interval, a different on-time, Steady light, and a text message. Each control changes the running board.
Change the initial interval here, and keep the header control default in sync. Plotter changes this variable while the program runs.
Up to 40 UTF-8 bytes plus a zero terminator. Received text is never executed as code.

Parse a signed whole number from valueStart through the end of the command. Reject empty text, non-digits and oversized values before changing any setting. Each handler also checks its own permitted range and step.
Fixed incoming line buffer, including room for a terminator. Charts, images and the JSON header stay on the computer/Flash, not in this array.

block.field: @msg Paused: LED off. Press Start to continue.
@msg LED disabled. Enable it to resume the selected pattern.
@msg Blink selected. Interval and on-time now change the light pattern.
@msg Steady light selected. Choose Blink to use interval and on-time again.
@msg A fresh blink cycle starts now.
@msg Interval changed. Watch the L LED blink faster or slower.
@msg Invalid period: use 100..2000 in steps of 100.
@msg On-time changed. Watch how long the L LED stays lit in each cycle.
@msg Invalid duty: use 10..90 in steps of 10.
@msg Use a single line of printable text.
@msg Message is too long: use at most 40 bytes.
@msg Unknown command. Use the controls shown by this sketch.
@msg Command too long; shorten it and try again.

block.comment: Read one complete newline-terminated command. Partial lines stay in a fixed byte buffer. CR is ignored; oversized commands are discarded. There is no String allocation or waiting for bytes. Expand this reusable function to see the ordinary array and logic blocks.
Confirm the values actually accepted by the board. JSON escaping preserves quotes and backslashes in the text control. This response updates the controls without sending another command.

block.comment: This is an ordinary Serial text message stored in Flash. Click it to edit formatted JSON. The computer creates instruments and computes derived fields; this sketch sends only input values.

block.field: @msg The L LED is already blinking. Try a slower interval, then Steady light. Type a message to hear back from the board.

block.comment: Send the layout, current accepted values and a useful next step. Called on boot and on START, so opening Plotter later still works.
Begin blinking immediately after upload. Announce the controls once here; Start also requests the current header and values.
Use elapsed milliseconds instead of delay. The command reader remains responsive between updates; unsigned subtraction also works when millis wraps.

Update the LED continuously without delay. The period is one full cycle; duty is its on percentage. Send a 20 Hz graph sample while running. Try changing controls one at a time and watch both the LED and the graph.
